page: Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in single-core CPU stress tests, text processing, and PassMark memory scores. Large-block memory bandwidth, both read and write, and single-threaded compression tasks register in the top 25% of tested servers. However, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations fall within the average tier. Large-model LLM inference is not supported due to the lack of GPU acceleration, though small-model text generation shows strong performance.

This server offers balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the premium of specialized memory or GPU hardware. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage makes it well-suited for general-purpose workloads, text processing pipelines, web serving, and moderate database operations.
